title: One Invoice per Order: Patient Invoices & Statements Account Structure
content:
Under Patient Invoices & Statements a patient holds one invoice per order and any number of invoices overall. The total number of invoices a patient may hold is not capped.

## Clauses

**1. Invoices held by a patient.** Each invoice records what the patient owes for one order, that is, one accession and one date of service. A patient with several orders therefore holds several invoices, and there is no ceiling on how many.

**2. No second invoice for an order.** An order never has a second invoice: every later posting for the same order is booked on its existing invoice. Whether an order already has an invoice is read from the laboratory's own invoice records for that same order, ahead of the posting, not from the caller's account of it. An invoice of the order in any status — open, on hold, on a payment plan, in collections, paid or closed — is that order's existing invoice.

**3. Statements and the open balance.** Statements are addressed per invoice. The patient's open balance is the total of the balance due on every one of the patient's invoices whose status is open, on hold, payment plan or collections. That open balance across invoices, and not the balance of any single invoice, is what Patient Payment Plans and the Patient Financial Assistance Program read.

## Which invoices enter the open balance

| Invoice status | Counted in the patient's open balance |
|---|---|
| Open | Yes |
| On hold | Yes |
| Payment plan | Yes |
| Collections | Yes |
| Paid | No |
| Closed | No |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical patient and amounts)

A patient holds five invoices, one for each of five orders:

| Invoice | Status | Balance due |
|---|---|---|
| A | Open | 85.00 |
| B | On hold | 140.00 |
| C | Payment plan | 312.50 |
| D | Paid | 0.00 |
| E | Closed | 0.00 |

The open balance is 85.00 plus 140.00 plus 312.50, a total of 537.50. Invoices D and E do not enter it. Statements, by contrast, are sent per invoice: invoice A receives its own statement showing 85.00, not 537.50.

If a further patient-responsibility amount is later assigned for the order billed on invoice D, it is booked on invoice D, because that order already has an invoice; no sixth invoice is opened for the order.
